summary: Alabama has no state law making smoke or CO alarms a condition of selling a one- or two-family home, and no statewide alarm requirement for existing houses at all; the only alarm duty found in the Code of Alabama applies to hotel guest rooms.
citation: No Alabama Code section found requiring smoke or CO alarms at sale or transfer of a one- or two-family dwelling. Closest related provisions located: Ala. Code 34-15-4 (hotel owners must install and maintain a battery or electrically operated smoke detector in each guest sleeping room, listed by a nationally recognized testing organization; history: Acts 1981, No. 81-290); Ala. Code 35-9A-204 (landlord's duty to maintain premises, which contains no smoke alarm provision; Act 2006-316).
notVerified: The absence of a requirement. This was established by full-text searching the Code of Alabama through the Alabama Legislature's own ALISON site and reading the candidate sections returned; the search engine is fuzzy and exact-phrase queries behaved inconsistently (a phrase search for "smoke alarm" returned zero results), so a relevant section could in principle have been missed. Treat 'no requirement at sale' as well supported but not exhaustively proven.

A 2019 bill, HB 426, would have added a landlord smoke-alarm maintenance duty to Ala. Code 35-9A-204. The current text of 35-9A-204 contains no smoke-alarm language, which indicates the bill did not become law, but its final disposition was not confirmed.

Whether the statewide residential construction code adopted by the Alabama Energy and Residential Codes Board (or any successor body) requires smoke or CO alarms in new or altered homes. A search of the Code of Alabama for the residential code returned nothing usable and the code itself was not read. New construction is a separate question from sale in any case.
The Alabama State Fire Marshal's administrative rules (Alabama Department of Insurance) were not reviewed.
Local Alabama city and county ordinances, which were not checked and may impose their own alarm or inspection requirements at sale.
